children: The Indonesian rupiah weakened toward IDR 17,700 per U.S. dollar on Tuesday, extending losses for a fourth straight session as the U.S. dollar index firmed ahead of the Fed’s policy decision later this week.

Locally, elevated oil prices heightened inflation concerns after headline figures accelerated to 3.19% in August. As a net oil importer, Indonesia remains vulnerable to higher global energy costs, which could add pressure to both inflation and the fiscal position.

On the policy front, Bank Indonesia is set to hold its policy meeting next week after keeping its key rate unchanged for a second consecutive month in August, following a cumulative 100bp tightening since May.
Meanwhile, Suahasil Nazara was sworn in as the new finance minister, replacing Purbaya Yudhi in a surprise reshuffle, the third change in less than two years.
Suahasil pledged budget discipline, including the 3% deficit cap, as external headwinds mount from rising U.S. Treasury yields and oil above $100 per barrel.

title: Rupiah Falls for 4th Session Amid Dollar, Oil Pressures
